summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinvijaya. He held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1945–1965), Gujarat University (1965–1975), and the L.D. Institute of Indology (~1973–2000).

Harjot Oberoi specializes in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College (~1973–1976), Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1976–1980), and the Australian National University (~1980–1987). Around 1987, he held the chair for Punjabi and Sikh studies at the University of British Columbia.
Harogadde Manappa Nayak was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin worked in linguistics. He studied at UC Berkeley (1943–1950) and Yale University (~1950–1955). He held faculty posts at Columbia (1955) and Yale (1962–1996), also serving as curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

Harold Edward Musson was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, and under traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana (~1949–1955). He served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Harold G. Coward, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earned his doctorate at McMaster University (~1969–1973). He was a professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992), directed its press (1981–1983), and was director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

Harold Hargreaves was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist. He served as headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar, Superintendent for the Archaeological Survey Frontier Province Peshawar (~1914–1928), and Superintendent and Deputy Director General for the Archaeological Survey of India between 1910 and 1931.

Harold Herman Bender worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lafayette College, Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and Berlin under Richard Pischel and Wilhelm Schulze. He was an assistant professor at Princeton University (1909–1950).

Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD ~1966–1969). He held positions at Valparaiso University, Masindi Senior Secondary School, and served as professor of humanities at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney.

Harold Walter Bailey specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under F. W. Thomas and R. P. Dewhurst. He held posts at SOAS (1929–1936) and Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani specialized in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University and Oxford, later training under Ghulam Yazdani. He held posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).

Harry Campbell Norman was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Edinburgh under Samuel Butcher, William Hardie, and Julius Eggeling, and at Oxford under Arthur Macdonell. In 1905, he became Professor of English Literature at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Harry Charles Purvis Bell, who worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studied at Cheltenham College in 1864 and joined the Ceylon Civil Service in 1873.

Harry Falk specializes in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gaya Charan Tripathi and Ulrich Schneider. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (~1978–1993) and served as professor and Director at the Free University of Berlin (1993–2012).
Harry Halén is a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Pentti Aalto and served as an amanuensis at the University of Helsinki.

Harsha Gautam is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Delhi University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Texas at Austin. She held posts at the National Museum, UT Austin, and the Metropolitan Museum of Art (2024–2025).

Harshit Mishra works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Delhi University, the International School for Jain Studies, Central Sanskrit University, and Ghent University. In 2024, he served as a Research Associate at the International School for Jain Studies.

Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi, and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).

Hartmut Scharfe was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Friedrich Weller and completed his doctorate under Paul Thieme, later holding a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.
